subjects.name: Law enforcement in the United States

summary: Behind the Police episode tracing how the Ku Klux Klan and American police overlapped, from Reconstruction-era sheriffs who rode with the first Klan to the 1920s Klan running police forces and the Red Summer of 1919.

evidence.note: Post-Civil War vagrancy laws and convict leasing enforced by local police open the narrative
First Klan founded in Pulaski, Tennessee in 1866
Union County, South Carolina: sheriff tied to a Klan cell leads the jail raid of January 1871
Grant, the Enforcement Acts and Akerman's federal prosecutions break the first Klan by 1872
Second Klan wins Anaheim council seats; Klan officers patrol in robes
Oregon Klan recruits police in Medford, partners with Portland police, helps elect a governor
Indiana Klan takes over the Horse Thief Detective Association; 1923 expulsion of Black residents
Phillips County, Arkansas massacre of Black sharecroppers with police backing
Modern segment: officers tied to the Klan and League of the South, 2012 to 2017 FBI document

notes: Primary subjects are both organizations, so roles are empty. Settings span SC, TN, CA, OR, IN, IL, AR and DC, so no single subdivision. covered_span ends 2017 with the FBI counterterrorism guide; 2020 Portland and Palmdale references are brief asides. main_span ends 1925 with the Indiana Klan membership peak. Theme primary could arguably be racism-white-supremacy.
